newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says weakening EMU would be wrong.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says weakening EMU would be wrong.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Thursday that any moves to weaken the strict fiscal targets for Europe's single currency would be wrong and have a negative impact on European economic and monetary union (EMU).
Waigel added that in long discussions with European finance ministers and politicians that there was no serious talk of weakening the critiera for EMU.
The strict EMU policies of the Bonn government and the Bundesbank have been criticised recently by former German chancellor Helmut Schmidt.
"Schmidt's criticism of us and (Bundesbank President Hans) Tietmeyer is misguided and wrong. Veering from the targets is not a question," Waigel told German radio.
He said any weakening of the EMU restrictions on budget deficits and public debt would raise expectations on financial markets that the single currency, the Euro, would be weaker than anticipated.

"In the last months and years in every European body there has been general agreement that the criteria would be applied strictly and uncompromisingly," Waigel said. "To veer from this now would be fundamentally wrong."
Waigel said that the three percent limit on budget deficits was an upper target that should under normal circumstances not be allowed to be exceeded.
Commenting on Germany's difficulties meeting the tough criteria contained in the Maastricht Treaty, he said: "We are moving in the right direction". -- Bonn Newsroom, 49 228 26097150
